== Old PC website (swccgpc.com) facts added, 24 November 2026 ==
Added from old swccgpc.com pages: the late-2002 Decktech partnership and the call for Young Jedi and Jedi Knights event volunteers ([https://web.archive.org/web/20040620161313/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds 2003]); the March 2003 Classic Format Subcommittee changes ([https://web.archive.org/web/20030824053912/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/classicnews03312003.htm 31 March 2003]); Duane Bruun as Squadron Member ([https://web.archive.org/web/20031229115404/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/may03archives.htm May 2003 updates]); the June 2004 advocate roles (New Advocates page, already cited); and the May 2006 call for volunteers ([https://web.archive.org/web/20060617220108/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8 sid=8]).
=== Missing data ===
* The Road to Worlds 2003 page carries no date; it says only "As the New Year approaches" and looks back on 2002. The citation gives "undated, late 2002".
* Left out: the role addresses (Classic Format Subcommittee, Duane Bruun) and Scott Lingrell's personal address in the 2006 post.

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* The June 2004 bullet dates the two new Player Advocates from the New Advocates page (Wayback, 3 June 2004); forum posters were congratulating Kevin Brownell and Nick Kolnik on 24 May 2004 after the main-site announcement, and their own pages give 24 May 2004.

=== Missing data ===
* No source found here for a Jedi Knights subcommittee's members beyond the forum signature of "Bubba Joe" (no full name).

* Left out: the 6 October 2003 shipping of the uncut-sheet prizes (already on [[Players Committee]]; not a change of structure).
* Left out: that "all virtual-card text would go into the upcoming rules documents" (April 2005). Carr's proxy post (p=72226) says the opposite: tracking altered text would mean putting every card text in the rulings documents, which he called unworkable.
* Left out: that Nick Kolnik had saved the collecting-thread pages Scott Lingrell reposted in December 2005 (the repost does not say who saved them).
* Left out: that the two design people "made most virtual cards" (May 2005); the source is a player's one-line answer naming Doug Taylor and Scott Lingrell only.
* Left out: a player's April 2006 remark that "Carr IS the PC right now", and Carr's 65-hour weeks (hearsay; the hours are not in the cited post). Kolnik's "NOT GOING BROKE" remark is not in the cited post either.
* Left out: the August 2008 swccgonline.com plans (an e-mail reply quoted by a player; the post does not show it was a PC project).
* The 15 July 2005 recap (p=88430) was captured in two topics (t=6375 and t=6561); cited once as pcf-6375-88430.
* Ref titles: some captures were taken with view=next / view=previous, which show a neighbouring topic; where the topic title of a post is not preserved, the ref uses a descriptive title.
